text.p: Sterling maintained its recent star billing in morning Europe, rising sharply to flirt with 20-month highs against the mark.
Dealers said sterling was being helped by a variety of factors, including the perception that the outlook for the UK economy was upbeat.
"The market is focusing on fundamentals and at the moment those look good," said UK economist Stuart Weatherby of Panmure Gordon in London.

Dealers said September producer price data due to be released at 0830 GMT would show a moderate picture for inflation, easing market anxieties after last week's retail price figures came in slightly higher than expected.
Finland's entry at the weekend into the European exchange rate mechanism had positive implications for sterling, analysts said.

They said the pound was being dragged up in line with EMU convergence trades, while at the same time it was being seen as a safe haven from any turmoil resulting from international debate over European monetary union.
Although sterling was seen as benefiting from the show of political unity at last week's Conservative party conference, analysts said politics was on balance being seen as a negative factor.
"With the reopening of parliament you are going to have a focus on government rifts and the debate on political sleaze," said Weatherby.
Sterling was trading at 0811 GMT in Europe at 2.4168/73 marks, just short of a 20-month high, while cable was at $1.5793/03, just off an 11-month high of $1.5825.
